items.content_html:
Value Prop

You can now access complete security advisory data directly through the GraphQL API, including fields like cveId, severity, url, and review timestamps. New filter arguments for severity and withdrawal status let you narrow results server-side, so your queries return exactly what you need without extra processing. If your integration is built on GraphQL, you no longer need to maintain a separate REST client just to read advisory information.

Expected Outcome

Developers and security teams who rely on GitHub GraphQL APIs can now build and maintain simpler, more efficient integrations for consuming security advisory data. Closing these gaps between the REST and GraphQL advisory APIs reduces unnecessary complexity, lowers rate-limit pressure, and removes a documented barrier to GraphQL-only workflows. The result is a more consistent API experience across GitHub security tooling.
items.title: More global security advisory data is now available in the GraphQL API [GA]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Code Quality scanning now works across multiple branches, not just your default branch. You can run scans on protected branches, release branches, or any branch that matters to your team's workflow. This gives you quality insights where and when you need them, regardless of where active development is happening.

Expected Outcome

Extending Code Quality scanning beyond the default branch helps teams catch issues earlier — before they reach main — and enforces consistent quality standards across all critical branches. Teams that rely on protected or long-lived branches gain the same visibility they've come to expect on their default branch, reducing the risk of quality regressions slipping through.
items.title: Multi-branch Code Quality scanning [Public Preview]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

You can now upload code coverage reports in more formats — including Go's native coverage format — directly to GitHub, without converting them first. This removes a manual, error-prone step that affected developers working with Go modules and other test frameworks that don't produce Cobertura XML. Broader format support means your coverage data reaches GitHub accurately, so you get reliable insights into test health across your repositories.

Expected Outcome

Expanding coverage report format support reduces friction for developers whose toolchains generate non-Cobertura output, making it easier to adopt GitHub's code coverage features without workarounds. Go native format support addresses the most-requested gap from public preview feedback, and accurate module path handling eliminates the basename collision issues introduced by third-party converters. The result is more teams getting complete, trustworthy coverage data with less setup effort.
items.title: Code coverage: expanded report format support [GA]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

With organization-level code coverage reporting, you can see test coverage metrics and trends across all repositories in your organization from a single view. This makes it easy to identify which repositories carry the most risk due to low test coverage and prioritize where to focus quality improvements. You get a clear, aggregated picture of your organization's testing health without having to check each repository individually.

Expected Outcome

Teams working to improve software quality gain the visibility they need to make informed decisions about where to invest in testing. By surfacing coverage trends over time, this feature helps engineering leaders and developers track progress toward quality goals at scale across their entire organization.
items.title: Code coverage: organization-level reporting [Public Preview]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Repository-level code coverage reporting gives you a clear view of your test coverage directly in the Code Quality tab, so you can instantly see how well your default branch is tested. A trend chart alongside the current coverage percentage makes it easy to understand whether coverage is improving, declining, or holding steady over time — without leaving GitHub.

Expected Outcome

Developers and engineering teams gain a single place to monitor test coverage health at the repository level, reducing the need for external tooling or manual reporting. By making coverage trends visible and accessible, teams can catch coverage regressions early and make more informed decisions about code quality investments.
items.title: Code coverage: repository-level reporting [Public Preview]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Code Quality rulesets now enforce checks on direct pushes to the default branch, not just on pull requests. This means the quality gates you configure actually protect your repository the way you expect — regardless of how code is introduced. You can trust that your default branch stays clean without having to rely on contributors always opening a pull request.

Expected Outcome

Developers and teams will have consistent, reliable enforcement of their Code Quality rules across all paths code can take into the default branch. Closing this gap removes a silent bypass that could allow unreviewed or low-quality code to land undetected, giving teams greater confidence in their branch protection configuration.
items.title: Code Quality rulesets block direct pushes to the default branch [GA]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Enterprise administrators can now disable Code Quality across their entire enterprise with a single action. This immediately turns off Code Quality in every repository and locks organization-level settings to prevent re-enablement, so administrators have clear, enforceable control over how the feature is adopted. Before fully evaluating Code Quality, admins can confidently ensure they are not being charged for it.

Expected Outcome

Enterprise administrators should be able to act quickly when they need to turn off Code Quality at scale, without manually adjusting settings across hundreds of organizations. Providing a single "Disable all" control removes the gap between what administrators expect the enterprise policy to do and what it actually does, eliminating unexpected billing. This builds trust that enterprise-level controls have immediate, complete effect across the organization hierarchy.
items.title: Enterprise-level disable all for Code Quality [Public Preview]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Code Quality now enforces billing requirements at enablement, so you only activate a paid feature when your organization has a valid payment method in place. This prevents unexpected usage that cannot be billed correctly, keeping your billing experience clean and predictable. Whether you're enabling Code Quality on a new repository or managing existing ones, you'll always have a clear, supported path from setup to payment.

Expected Outcome

As Code Quality moves out of free preview, this change ensures the feature operates within a proper billing relationship for every repository and organization that uses it. Existing repositories enabled during the preview without a billing path will be cleaned up, and future enablement is gated on a valid payment method. This creates a consistent, trustworthy experience where feature access and billing are always aligned.
items.title: Billing prerequisites for enabling Code Quality [GA]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Your Code Quality settings now do exactly what they say. Whether you've enabled Code Quality across your organization or turned it off entirely, those settings are consistently enforced across every repository — including ones restored from deletion or enabled through the API. You're only billed for Code Quality when it's actually running.

Expected Outcome

Customers should be able to trust that organization-level Code Quality controls are the single source of truth for what runs and what gets billed. This release reconciles repositories already affected by the inconsistencies, so existing organizations will see their enforced settings take effect without any manual intervention.
items.title: Code Quality enablement and disablement reliability fixes [GA]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

GitHub Enterprise Server 3.23 brings the latest developer innovations directly to your on-premises environment through a quarterly release cycle. This release ensures your team can access new features and improvements at a predictable cadence, keeping your enterprise deployment current with GitHub's platform roadmap.

Expected Outcome

We're delivering this quarterly release to maintain feature parity between GitHub.com and Enterprise Server, enabling enterprise customers to adopt new capabilities and security improvements on their own timeline. This regular release cycle demonstrates our commitment to providing enterprise teams with continuous access to platform innovations.
items.title: GitHub Enterprise Server 3.23 [GA]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Multi-disk storage for MySQL is now the default configuration for new GitHub Enterprise Server installations, helping your instance handle high-traffic loads more efficiently. This configuration reduces database bottlenecks and improves overall performance without requiring manual setup.

Expected Outcome

By standardizing multi-disk MySQL configuration on new installs, we're proactively reducing the scalability challenges that many customers experience as their GitHub Enterprise instance grows. This change helps teams maintain consistent performance during peak usage periods and minimizes the need for database optimization work after deployment.
items.title: Multi-disk as default on new installs [GA]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

With shared Copilot automations, your team can collaboratively build automations that work for everyone in your repository. Instead of each developer creating their own personal automations, your team can define shared workflows—like standardized standup updates or common code reviews—that Copilot executes consistently across the team. AI credit usage is billed to your repository, and the automation runs as the "Copilot" identity, keeping your workflows team-owned rather than individual-dependent.

Expected Outcome

We're enabling teams to automate repetitive tasks and common workflows across the entire SDLC, allowing your team to focus on high-impact work. By making automations shareable and centrally managed, teams can scale automation practices across the repository and deliver completed work more quickly without the overhead of each person maintaining their own automations.
items.title: Automate work for your team with shared Copilot automations [GA]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Reachability analysis for Dependabot helps you cut through alert noise by identifying which dependency vulnerabilities are actually reachable from your code — so you can focus remediation efforts on the issues that pose a real risk. Starting with JavaScript, which accounts for the majority of Dependabot alerts in enterprise environments, you get clearer signal on which alerts demand immediate attention and which can be deprioritized.

Expected Outcome

Developers and security teams spend less time triaging Dependabot alerts and more time fixing the vulnerabilities that actually matter. By surfacing exploitability context directly in the alert experience, reachability analysis helps organizations reduce noise, improve prioritization accuracy, and build more confident, efficient security workflows.
items.title: Reachability Analysis for Dependabot [Public Preview]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

You can now view and act on your security work directly inside GitHub Copilot — no browser tab-switching required. Type /security in Copilot App or CLI to open a security canvas that brings your assigned alerts, campaign work, and prioritized security items into a single, unified inbox. Filter, triage, and work through security findings organized by risk and relevance, right where you already code.

Expected Outcome

Security alerts today are scattered across scanner-specific pages, making it hard for developers to know what to fix first. By surfacing prioritized security work inside Copilot App and CLI, developers can discover and address vulnerabilities without breaking their flow. The goal is to reduce context-switching and help teams close security gaps faster by meeting developers where they already work.
items.title: Security extension for the Copilot App [Public Preview]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Stacked pull requests let you break large changes into small, focused, independently reviewable units — so reviews move faster and nothing blocks your team. Each pull request in the stack can be reviewed and validated on its own, and when everything looks good, you can merge the entire stack in one click. Whether you're working solo or collaborating with coding agents, stacked pull requests give you a structured way to ship complex work quickly and incrementally.

Expected Outcome

As more code is generated at higher velocity — including by AI agents — code review has become the primary bottleneck to shipping. Stacked pull requests reach general availability to give every developer on GitHub a reliable, scalable way to keep reviews manageable and momentum high. The goal is to make incremental, high-quality shipping the default experience, not the exception.
items.title: Stacked Pull Requests [GA]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Cloud sandboxes give GitHub Copilot a fast, secure, and stateful compute environment that powers agentic tasks across the tools you already use — including Slack, Microsoft Teams, and Jira. With snapshot and resume capabilities, Copilot can pick up where it left off without rebuilding context, making agent interactions faster and more reliable. This means less waiting and more time focused on the work that matters.

Expected Outcome

Developers get noticeably more responsive Copilot experiences as agents no longer need to repeatedly recreate their environment from scratch. By providing on-demand compute that starts quickly and preserves state across interactions, cloud sandboxes remove a key source of friction in agentic workflows. The result is a smoother, more interactive Copilot experience that scales across surfaces and use cases.
items.title: Cloud sandboxes [GA]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Copilot code review now uses secret scanning, including GitHub's purpose-built model for secret detection, in code review scans. This helps you catch sensitive credentials without the overhead of managing multiple detection tools.

Expected Outcome

We're improving the security posture of code reviews by embedding secret scanning, catching credential leaks at review time. This integration makes it easier for teams to maintain secure-by-default practices and reduces the risk of accidental secret exposure in pull requests.
items.title: Copilot code review includes secret scanning [Public Preview]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

When a secret like a Slack or Salesforce token is exposed in your repository, you can now revoke it with a single click directly from the secret scanning alert. This eliminates the need to track down the token owner or navigate complex support processes—GitHub handles revocation with the issuer for you.

Expected Outcome

We're making secret remediation faster and more autonomous for development teams. By reducing the friction to revoke exposed credentials, we help teams contain security breaches within minutes rather than hours, strengthening their overall security posture and reducing the risk window for potential misuse.
items.title: 1-click revocation for secret scanning partner types [Public Preview]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Security teams can now jump directly to any public monitoring alert with a shareable URL, making it faster to return to specific findings during triage or incident response. Teammates can bookmark alerts or quickly pull up the exact alert you're discussing without hunting through the full alert list.

Expected Outcome

Public monitoring alerts become easier to navigate and discuss, reducing friction in security team workflows. By giving alerts individual URLs, teams can establish a shared reference point for each finding, streamlining collaboration and reducing duplicate investigation efforts.
items.title: Public monitoring alerts now have direct links [GA]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Dependabot continues to stay on top of security vulnerabilities in your repositories, even as our alert volume grows. When your repository hasn't received any commits in a year, we automatically move your alerts to storage that's optimized for historical records—keeping Dependabot responsive for active projects while preserving your security history if you need to review it.

Expected Outcome

This change ensures Dependabot can continue issuing alerts at scale without outgrowing our infrastructure. By archiving alerts for inactive repositories, we free up resources to keep security scanning fast and reliable for repositories that are actively maintained, which is where developers need real-time insights most.
items.title: Dependabot alerts on inactive repos on github.com move to cold storage [GA]
